options: The Azure Monitor agent isn't sending Heartbeat because it's superseded by Metrics; switch to legacy MMA to restore Heartbeat.
The VM isn't linked to the workspace; re-onboard the VM to the correct Log Analytics workspace.
The Log Analytics workspace retention is too short; increase workspace retention to at least 30 days.
The DCR doesn't route the Heartbeat stream; add the "Microsoft-Heartbeat" stream to the DCR's dataFlows and publish it.
concept_mcqs.explanation: The DCR routes Performance and InsightsMetrics streams but not Heartbeat. Azure Monitor agent emits Heartbeat only if the DCR includes the Microsoft-Heartbeat stream. Adding that stream and applying the DCR will populate Heartbeat for the VM.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A: Retention affects historical data, not live ingestion. The query is for the last hour. B: AMA does support Heartbeat; it's controlled by DCR streams. D: VM Insights shows the workspace link is fine; missing is the specific Heartbeat stream routing.

concept_mcqs.stem:
A VM backup job finished with the following report:
```text
Job Type: Azure VM Backup
VM: sql-prod-01
App-consistent snapshot: Failed (VSS Writer SQLServerWriter timed out)
Crash-consistent snapshot: Completed
Restore point: 2026-06-18T02:00:12Z (Crash-consistent)
```
You restore to a new VM and start SQL Server. Which outcome should you expect, and why?
options: SQL Agent jobs and system databases are restored but user databases are skipped because the snapshot wasn't app-consistent.

The restore will succeed; SQL will roll back/forward to the last checkpoint, yielding a transactionally consistent database as of that checkpoint but potentially losing the most recent in-flight transactions.
The restore will fail because Azure Backup requires an app-consistent snapshot for any database workload.
The database will have torn pages requiring forced recovery and manual DBCC; crash-consistent snapshots are unusable for SQL Server.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Crash-consistent VM backups capture a file-system–consistent point. On startup, SQL Server recovery replays/rolls back to the last checkpoint, resulting in a consistent state as of that checkpoint. You may lose data since the most recent checkpoint, but the restore doesn't inherently fail.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: App-consistency is preferred but not required; crash-consistent restores are supported. C: Torn pages are not expected as a rule; SQL recovery protects against this in most cases. D: VM-level backup doesn't selectively skip user DB files based on VSS outcome; it captured the disks.

options: Create a new vault in the paired region and copy existing backup items into it.
Enable Cross Region Restore on the vault and switch storageModelType to GeoRedundant.
Enable ZoneRedundant storage and leave Cross Region Restore disabled.
Move the existing vault to the paired region, then restore from there.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Cross-region restore requires vault storage redundancy to be GRS and the CRR feature enabled. LRS cannot restore to the paired region.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: ZRS doesn't support cross-region restore. C: You cannot move a Recovery Services vault across regions. D: You cannot copy backup items between vaults; restore requires GRS with CRR.

options: The manual action executes automatically during unplanned failover to speed up recovery.
All machines start simultaneously because unplanned failovers ignore group order.
dc-01 and sql-01 start first; ASR waits for the DB-and-Infra group to complete before starting app-01 and app-02.
app-01 and app-02 are included in the same multi-VM consistency snapshot as sql-01 due to the replicationGroup setting.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Failover plan groups are executed sequentially. Group-level manual actions require operator confirmation; they don't auto-run. Only sql-01 is in a multi-VM consistency group (with others in that group), not the app VMs.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: Manual actions are prompts; they don't run themselves. C: Group order is honored in unplanned failover. D: Only VMs in the same replicationGroup share a crash-consistent snapshot; app VMs aren't included.

options: It is suppressed by the processing rule; no action groups fire and the alert is marked as suppressed.
It is not suppressed because Alert Processing Rules don't apply to Sev3; only Sev4 is suppressed.
It is suppressed only if the alert rule was created after the processing rule; older rules are unaffected.
It fires action groups but is hidden in the Alerts blade until 03:00 UTC.
concept_mcqs.explanation: The rule targets Sev3 and Sev4 within the specified time window at the resource group scope. The alert is suppressed and action groups do not execute.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: Suppression blocks notifications; the alert still appears with a suppressed state, not hidden until a time. C: Processing rules apply regardless of alert rule creation time. D: The rule explicitly includes Sev3.

options: They are marked non-compliant; backup isn't enabled until a remediation task runs with a managed identity to deploy the fix.
They are immediately protected by backup; deployIfNotExists auto-deploys on existing resources without extra steps.
They are denied start/stop operations until backup is enabled because the policy blocks the control plane for non-compliant VMs.
They are ignored; deployIfNotExists only applies to resources created after the assignment time.
concept_mcqs.explanation: deployIfNotExists evaluates compliance but requires a remediation task to perform the deployment on already-existing resources. Without remediation, they remain non-compliant and unprotected.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: A: No auto-deployment occurs on existing resources without remediation. C: Policy evaluates both existing and new resources. D: There's no deny effect here; start/stop isn't blocked by deployIfNotExists.

concept_mcqs.stem:
You run this KQL to detect storage latency issues:
```text
Perf
| where ObjectName == "LogicalDisk" and CounterName == "Avg. Disk sec/Write"
| where InstanceName !in ("_Total", "HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy*")
| summarize p95 = percentile(CounterValue, 95) by Computer, bin(TimeGenerated, 15m)
| where p95 > 0.02
```
Which statement best describes what it flags?
options: 15-minute windows where the 95th percentile write latency exceeded 20 ms on any logical disk per computer.
5-minute windows where the 95th percentile read latency exceeded 20 ms on all disks.
15-minute windows where the average write throughput exceeded 20 MB/s on any disk.
Any single sample exceeding 20 ms latency, regardless of windowing.
concept_mcqs.explanation: CounterName is Avg. Disk sec/Write (write latency). The query bins data into 15-minute windows and filters where the 95th percentile exceeds 0.02 seconds (20 ms).
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: It's latency in seconds, not throughput. C: It's write latency, not read, and the bin is 15 minutes. D: The filter is on the 95th percentile over the window, not single samples.

options: Logs are dropped because sending the same category twice violates diagnostic settings limits.
Duplicate logs are ingested for VMGuestMetrics, inflating cost and potentially confusing queries.
Azure Monitor deduplicates identical categories to the same workspace, so there is no impact.
Only the newest diagnostic setting is honored; the older is auto-disabled.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Multiple diagnostic settings can send the same category to the same destination, and Azure Monitor does not deduplicate; duplicates are ingested and billed.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: There is no deduplication across diagnostic settings. C: Azure doesn't auto-disable older settings. D: It's supported; logs aren't dropped for duplication.

concept_mcqs.stem:
Role assignments for a user are:
```text
User: ops.alex@contoso.com
- Subscription "Prod-Sub": Monitoring Reader
- Resource group "rg-app": Reader
- Log Analytics workspace "law-prod": Log Analytics Reader
```
Which action will be blocked for this user?
options: Query the Heartbeat table in law-prod.
View an existing metric alert rule in rg-app.
Create a new Action Group in rg-app for on-call notifications.
Pin the existing Alerts workbook to the Azure Portal dashboard.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Creating or updating Action Groups requires Monitoring Contributor at the scope. Monitoring Reader permits viewing but not creating. Log Analytics Reader permits querying the workspace.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: Monitoring Reader allows viewing alert rules. C: Log Analytics Reader allows querying tables. D: Pinning existing workbooks is allowed with read permissions.

options: A synthetic point is created from the nearest Sunday; you can restore to 2026-05-31 and Azure will roll forward to 05-29.
The weekly retention keeps every Friday for 12 weeks, so the point is available.
The monthly retention keeps all days in May for 12 months, so the point is available.
No restore point for 2026-05-29; the daily point expired after 30 days and it's neither a weekly Sunday nor a last Sunday of the month.
concept_mcqs.explanation: Daily retention of 30 days has expired by 2026-06-29. Weekly retention keeps only Sundays; monthly keeps only the last Sunday. Friday 2026-05-29 matches none of these.
concept_mcqs.distractor_rationale: B: Weekly retention targets Sunday backups only. C: Monthly retention targets the last Sunday only, not all days. D: Azure Backup doesn't synthesize intermediate days from weekly/monthly points.

scenario_questions.scenario: Contoso runs a 3-tier payment app in East US: two App Service instances behind Azure Front Door, two Windows VMs for APIs (app-01, app-02), and a SQL Server VM (sql-01) with disks in a Premium SSD zone-redundant configuration. Key Vault holds connection strings. Private endpoints are used for Key Vault and Storage. Azure Backup protects app and DB VMs with the policy in the prod Recovery Services vault (GRS + Cross Region Restore enabled). Azure Site Recovery (ASR) replicates app-01/app-02 and sql-01 to Central US; a failover plan groups sql-01 first, then app VMs. DNS is in Azure DNS. Log Analytics collects Heartbeat, Perf, and SQL ErrorLog via AMA with alerts on Heartbeat missing and SQL severity >= 20. Compliance requires RTO <= 2 hours, RPO <= 15 minutes for the database.
scenario_questions.task: Design the end-to-end disaster recovery sequence for a region-wide outage of East US. Specify the exact failover steps, how you will handle private endpoints/DNS, how to re-establish Key Vault access, and how you will validate data freshness against the RPO. Include how you would fail back when East US returns. Justify your choices for each step with respect to the stated RTO/RPO and monitoring signals.
scenario_questions.expected_answer: A strong answer sequences: 1) Declare disaster and freeze changes; 2) Validate last replicated point for sql-01 (check ASR latest recovery point timestamp and SQL error log in Log Analytics) meets 15-min RPO; 3) Execute ASR unplanned failover with plan order: sql-01 group then app-01/app-02; confirm boot success; 4) Update or preconfigure network mappings in ASR to Central US VNets; 5) Recreate private endpoints in Central US for Key Vault/Storage or switch to globally reachable endpoints with proper firewall rules, ensuring Key Vault access policies/managed identities are valid in target subscription/region; 6) Update DNS records or Front Door origin to point to Central US endpoints; set low TTLs in advance; 7) Validate application by running synthetic probes, KQL queries confirming Heartbeat present for all components and no new SQL severity >=20 since failover; 8) Communicate recovery complete within 2 hours. For failback: enable reverse replication from Central US to East US, run planned failover back after catching up, reverse DNS/Front Door changes, and decommission temporary private endpoints; document and test backups created during the outage are cataloged; ensure Key Vault references and managed identities work post-failback. Justify that ASR provides near-15-minute RPO for the VMs and that SQL recovery to latest recovery point plus transaction log integrity checks meet the requirement. Emphasize pre-created runbooks, automation for DNS/Front Door switch, and alert thresholds to detect any drift beyond RPO before executing.

rubric.criterion: Sequenced failover steps aligned to plan order (DB first, then app) and use of ASR constructs
Clear handling of private endpoints/Key Vault access (recreate or route, firewall, identity)
DNS/Front Door cutover approach with TTL strategy and rollback plan
RPO/RTO validation using ASR recovery point timestamps and monitoring signals (KQL/alerts)
Failback plan including reverse replication and config rollback

scenario_questions.scenario: You inherited a noisy monitoring setup. VM guest metrics, Azure Activity Logs, and SQL diagnostics from 60 resources are all sent to a single workspace with 90-day retention. Engineers miss real issues due to alert floods. The monthly Log Analytics ingestion bill spiked 60% after enabling SQL diagnostics at Verbose. Some teams need detailed Perf/Logs; others just need availability SLOs.
scenario_questions.task: Propose a monitoring redesign that reduces alert noise and cost while preserving detection for real incidents. Specify: data collection rules and their scopes (which streams go where), table-level retention or archive for high-volume categories, alerting patterns (log vs metric alerts, dynamic thresholds), use of action groups and alert processing rules to route/suppress, and a plan to test changes without losing coverage.
scenario_questions.expected_answer: A strong answer partitions ingestion by need. Examples: create two DCRs — "platform-baseline" to collect Heartbeat + minimal Perf to a central workspace for all prod scopes; and "deep-dive-sql" to collect SQL ErrorLog, waits, and perf counters only for tagged SQL resources. Set table-level retention (e.g., Perf 30 days, SQL telemetry 14 days, archive high-volume verbose tables) and disable Verbose categories not used. Use metric alerts for CPU, memory (VM Insights) with dynamic thresholds and log alerts for rare errors (SQL severity >=20, Heartbeat missing). Introduce per-team Action Groups and route with alert processing rules; suppress Sev3/Sev4 during maintenance windows by schedule/tag. Validate in a staging workspace first, enabling workspace transformations to drop fields and sampling as appropriate; run parallel alerts and compare missed-incident rate over two weeks before cutover.

rubric.criterion: Clear DCR design separating baseline vs deep-dive streams with scoping/tags
Retention/archiving strategy at table/category level tied to cost impact
Alerting design using the right signal type and dynamic thresholds to reduce noise
Routing/suppression with action groups and processing rules, plus a safe testing/migration plan

scenario_questions.scenario: Finance requires 7-year retention for backups of two databases on sql-01. Other workloads may use 30-day backups. Currently, all VMs are protected by a single Daily+Weekly+Monthly policy in one Recovery Services vault. Soft delete is enabled. There is no immutable vault lock and no separation of duties; the same ops team both administers backups and manages the VMs.
scenario_questions.task: Design a compliant backup architecture and process that meets the 7-year requirement only for finance DBs while keeping other workloads on short retention. Include: vault/policy structure, use of item-level retention/policy assignment, immutable vault or MUA protections, key management/encryption, and test-restore practices to prove recoverability over long retention. Explain how you will prevent accidental or malicious deletion of long-retained backups.
scenario_questions.expected_answer: Expected: Split policies by retention. Either keep one vault with multiple policies (Finance-7y and Default-30d) or use a dedicated vault for finance with immutable protection (Enable Immutable vault + soft delete + MUA). Protect sql-01 with Azure VM backup for OS/disks and use workload-aware backup (SQL in Azure VM) for finance DBs with 7-year retention and GFS schedule; other VMs/databases stay on 30-day VM-level backups. Enable vault immutability and possibly multi-user authorization for critical operations; enforce Azure Policy to require assignment to correct policy for tagged finance resources; separate roles so backup admins cannot delete protected items (least privilege). Use customer-managed keys (if required) and document key rotation. Perform quarterly test restores of finance DB backups into an isolated subscription, logging evidence of restore times and data integrity checks. Ensure soft delete cannot be disabled without security approval.

rubric.criterion: Correct policy/vault design to isolate 7-year retention from 30-day workloads
Controls for immutability/soft delete/MUA and RBAC separation of duties
Use of SQL workload backup vs VM backup and justification for finance DBs
Test-restore cadence and evidence collection for compliance

scenario_questions.scenario: During a DR drill, you failed over app-01/app-02 and sql-01 to Central US. Synthetic probes pass, but users report intermittent 401 errors. Logs show Managed Identity token acquisition failures from app-01 when calling Key Vault. In DR, you recreated private endpoints in Central US and updated DNS. Key Vault firewall is set to selected networks, allowing only East US subnets. Alerts on Heartbeat and CPU show healthy; no errors in SQL.
scenario_questions.task: Diagnose the likely root cause and propose the minimal, secure fix. Include how to validate the fix in monitoring and how to bake this into the recovery plan so it doesn’t recur.
scenario_questions.expected_answer: Root cause: Key Vault firewall/network ACLs allow only East US subnets; DR VMs in Central US cannot reach Key Vault via new private endpoint or are blocked by firewall. Minimal secure fix: update Key Vault network rules to include Central US subnets used in DR (prefer pre-provisioning with disabled private endpoints and pre-approved subnets), or use a Key Vault private endpoint in Central US with proper DNS zone links. Validate by KQL querying app logs for token acquisition success and Key Vault diagnostics for successful Authorize/SecretGet events, and watching the 401 rate drop; add a health probe that checks a dummy secret read. Update DR plan to include step to switch DNS for the Key Vault private endpoint and confirm Key Vault firewall entries for DR subnets, with an approval checkpoint.

rubric.criterion: Correct identification of Key Vault network ACL/private endpoint scope as the cause
Proposed minimal and secure remediation (network rules/DR private endpoint plus DNS)
Validation steps using monitoring signals/logs to confirm recovery
Change to the recovery plan/runbook to prevent recurrence

practical_tasks.title: Produce a tested Disaster Recovery plan for a multi-tier workload
practical_tasks.brief: Create a recovery plan document for a representative 3-tier app hosted in Azure that you can access (your sandbox or provided lab). The plan must be executable by another engineer and include validation and rollback. Use Azure-native services only (Azure Backup and/or ASR). Run at least one tabletop or lab drill and incorporate evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture section with diagram or inventory listing components, regions, VNets/subnets, private endpoints, and dependencies (Key Vault, Storage, DNS).
Documented RTO/RPO targets and mapping to chosen protections (backup policies, ASR replication settings).

Step-by-step failover runbook covering order of operations (DB first, app next), DNS/Front Door or Traffic Manager changes, private endpoint/DNS zone steps, identity/Key Vault access checks, and validation probes.
Explicit rollback/failback steps, including reverse replication, data reconciliation approach, and DNS reversal.
Monitoring and verification section with at least two KQL queries (e.g., Heartbeat freshness, SQL error severity) and screenshots of successful checks post-failover.
Evidence of a drill: screenshots or logs from a test restore or ASR test failover, including timestamps that demonstrate whether the plan met RTO/RPO.
Controls and compliance: how soft delete/immutability is set, and RBAC assignments showing separation of duties for backup/DR.

rubric.criterion: Completeness and clarity of architecture and dependency mapping
RTO/RPO mapping to controls (backup/ASR) and justification
Runbook correctness and sequencing including DNS/private endpoints/Key Vault
Monitoring validation (quality of KQL, evidence that checks run and pass)
Failback/rollback path and drill evidence demonstrating feasibility

practical_tasks.title: Build a monitored Azure environment with actionable alerts and a dashboard
practical_tasks.brief: Configure Azure Monitor for a small environment you control (at minimum: 1 VM and 1 PaaS resource such as Key Vault, Storage, or App Service). Use the Azure Monitor agent and Data Collection Rules. Route resource diagnostics appropriately. Create alert rules, action groups, a suppression rule, and at least one Workbook. Prove it works by triggering a benign alert.
acceptance_criteria: One Log Analytics workspace with at least one Data Collection Rule collecting Heartbeat and a small set of Perf counters for the VM.
At least one resource diagnostic setting sending logs to the workspace (e.g., Key Vault AuditEvent or AppServiceHTTPLogs).
At least three alert rules: one metric (e.g., VM CPU), one log-based (e.g., Heartbeat missing), and one service log (e.g., Key Vault SecretGet failures), all targeting an Action Group.
An Alert Processing Rule that suppresses low-severity alerts during a defined maintenance window for your resource group.
A Workbook or Dashboard summarizing VM availability (Heartbeat) and one resource-specific metric/log, with a screenshot.
Evidence the system works: a screenshot of a fired alert and corresponding notification (email/webhook), plus a KQL query returning the underlying signal.
Exported ARM/Bicep/JSON templates of the DCR, diagnostic settings, alert rules, action group, and processing rule.

rubric.criterion: Workspace, DCR, and diagnostic settings correctly configured and scoped
Quality and diversity of alert rules with proper routing to action groups
Effective suppression rule and demonstration that it applies as intended
Useful workbook/dashboard presenting availability and a resource-specific insight
Working evidence (fired alert + query) and exported IaC artifacts
